learning_outcomes.text: Know, understand and use representation systems, as well as common conventions and standards in industrial design.
Be able to read, interpret and correctly execute industrial drawings, as well as graphically express ideas and designs in a standardized, clear and precise manner.
Be able to use computer-aided design applications for drawing elaboration.
Represent different types of parts and dimension them respecting technical drawing standards.
Be able to work in a team, apply critical reasoning, make decisions and communicate knowledge and conclusions in the field of industrial engineering.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Graphic Expression in Engineering and the Technical Drawing.
teaching_methods: Classroom presentation of concepts and problem-solving, group discussion sessions.
Laboratory activities of increasing difficulty to develop problem-solving autonomy.
Personal study, report writing, practical exercises, etc. as independent student work.
assessment_rules: Student results are graded on a numerical scale of 0 to 10. A score of 0-4.9 is Fail, 5.0-6.9 is Pass, 7.0-8.9 is Good, and 9.0-10 is Excellent. For continuous assessment, block A (Dihedral System), block B (Standardization and Visualization), and block C (Computer-Aided Representation) are weighted at 40%, 40%, and 20% respectively. A minimum score of 3.5 in each block is required to average the scores, and a total score of 5 or higher passes the course. In ordinary and extraordinary exams, students can either maintain scores of 5 or higher from continuous assessment and retake only blocks with lower scores (requiring a minimum of 3.5 per block to average), or choose to retake the entire course material, in which case no minimum score per block applies for averaging. The same block weights (40%, 40%, 20%) apply for these retake options.
